outputs.rationale: Ranked by shared latent pattern of using integral representations or Fourier-type transforms to simplify double integrals of special functions into closed-form expressions in fewer variables.

Ranked by latent similarity in reasoning pattern: problems that use a clever algebraic/combinatorial identity involving sums of powers to derive a clean extremal or number-theoretic result rank highest, followed by inequality/optimization problems with a constraint, while problems relying on purely structural, probabilistic, or group-theoretic reasoning rank lowest.

Ranked by latent relevance to the core reasoning pattern of counting equivalence classes under a combinatorial group-like action, prioritizing problems that define nontrivial equivalence relations on structured objects and enumerate the resulting classes.

Ranked by latent similarity to the query's eureka insight that transitivity/structural constraints on a convex body force it to be a canonical affine ball, prioritizing problems about convex geometry characterization (G.32), geometric constraint propagation (2013 pentagon), boundary-behavior-determining-structure (2016 M-function), and rigidity-under-constraints (2006 analytic maps), while problems from substantially different domains (probability, combinatorial number theory, kinematics) descend.

Ranked by descending latent relevance to mixtilinear incircle geometry and R/r inequalities — candidates directly defining or deriving properties of mixtilinear incircles (11774, 11900, 11386) first, then those sharing the same tangent-to-circumcircle construction (3887), then triangle-center/R-r inequality problems (10955), then general triangle-incircle geometry (12357, 10703, 10693), then tangentially related or completely different domains.

Ranked by latent relevance to the query's core pattern: recognizing binomial-coefficient generating functions and interchanging sums to evaluate a series involving a remainder term, with closest matches involving combinatorial series manipulation, binomial-sum convergence structure, and derivative-generating expansions.

Ranked by latent relevance to the core pattern of asymptotic tail analysis of distributions and limit theorems combining probability with asymptotic expansions, prioritizing problems sharing the 'aha' of understanding how distribution tails and probabilistic structure determine limiting behavior.

Ranked by latent relevance to the core pattern of exact definite integral/series evaluation to closed forms involving π via series expansions and special function identities, with integrals related to arctan, log, and gamma functions ranked highest, followed by problems using complex analysis or integral manipulation, and finally problems from disparate subfields with no shared reasoning structure.

Problems requiring Plancherel's identity or L^2 isometry of the Fourier transform are most relevant, followed by those using integral representations of analytic functions and L^2 spectral/approximation arguments; combinatorial and geometric problems without analytic L^2 structure are least relevant.
Ranked by how directly the problem requires solving a linear constant-coefficient ODE/system via its characteristic polynomial, which is the core algebraic pattern behind y''-2y'+y=0.

Ranked by latent relevance to the core insight of representing Riemann zeta values via clever integral transforms, with top documents sharing the same contour-integration/special-function-to-zeta reasoning pattern, while the rest are progressively less related to that specific eureka.

Ranked by latent relevance to the Riemann mapping theorem + Schwarz lemma (Schwarz-Pick) combo: problems involving holomorphic derivative bounds at fixed points or on the unit disc first, then other complex analysis, then structurally parallel existence-of-equivalence problems, then unrelated fields.

outputs.headline: Model struggles significantly on oblique verification, with mean nDCG@10 of just 0.09 and only 2 of 12 queries retrieving any gold document.
